title: ECB Holds Deposit Rate at 2.50% on October 29
description: The ECB left its three key policy rates unchanged: deposit facility 2.50%, main refinancing operations 2.65% and marginal lending facility 2.90%.
longFormSummary:
The Governing Council left the ECB’s three key interest rates unchanged on 29 October 2026. The deposit facility remains at 2.50%, the main refinancing operations rate at 2.65%, and the marginal lending facility at 2.90%.

The decision cites upside inflation risks and downside growth risks from energy prices. Future decisions remain dependent on incoming data, with no commitment to a particular rate path. APP and PEPP portfolios continue to decline as principal repayments are no longer reinvested.

The pin’s earlier prediction was a hold; the published decision confirms that outcome. Earlier market odds were a dated forecast rather than the decision itself.

title: September US PCE Inflation Reaches 3.6%; Core at 3.1%
description: BEA reports September PCE prices rose 0.5% on the month and 3.6% from a year earlier; core prices rose 0.3% monthly and 3.1% yearly.
longFormSummary:
September’s personal consumption expenditures price index rose 0.5% from August and 3.6% from a year earlier. Excluding food and energy, prices rose 0.3% monthly and 3.1% yearly. These are the monthly release’s measures, distinct from the quarterly GDP price measures published the same morning.

Personal income increased 0.2% and nominal consumer spending increased 0.5%. Real spending rose less than 0.1%, while real disposable personal income fell 0.3%. The personal saving rate was 3.8%. BEA also revised earlier monthly estimates; this pin now records the released September figures rather than its earlier calendar placeholder.

title: US GDP Grows 3.4% in Q3 2026 as Investment and Consumers Lift Output
description: BEA’s advance estimate puts third-quarter real GDP growth at a 3.4% annual rate, up from 2.2% in Q2. The initial estimate is subject to revision.
longFormSummary:
• The first estimate of US output for July–September 2026 shows real GDP rising at a 3.4% seasonally adjusted annual rate. The comparable second-quarter pace was 2.2%. This annualized figure is different from the quarter’s 0.8% nonannualized change.
  • Investment, household spending and government demand contributed to growth; falling exports and rising imports offset part of those gains. Underlying private domestic demand, measured by real final sales to private domestic purchasers, rose 4.9% annualized after 4.6% in Q2.
  • AP reports that the result exceeded a 3% FactSet forecast. Its coverage identifies AI-related equipment investment and consumers as supports, while housing investment fell 3.3%. This is an uneven expansion across sectors rather than evidence that every household or industry gained equally.
  • The publisher charts distinguish real output growth, component contributions in percentage points and quarterly annualized price changes. They retain the original units and source credit; the quarterly PCE chart is not September’s separate monthly inflation print.
  • BEA schedules the second Q3 estimate for November 25 and the third for December 23. Later releases can revise this initial reading.
dateConfidenceReasoning: BEA release dateline states 8:30 a.m. EDT Thursday October 29, 2026 (12:30 UTC).

title: Amazon Cuts About 250 Devices and Services Jobs on October 28
description: Amazon confirmed a new devices-and-services layoff round. Reuters reports about 250 affected roles, primarily in software development; the company did not publish an exact count.
longFormSummary:
• Amazon eliminated roles in its devices and services organization on October 28, 2026. The company confirmed the round to Reuters. The report puts the number at about 250, based on a person familiar with the matter, and says software development was the main area affected; Amazon itself did not provide a numerical total.
  • Workers received notifications that morning following a review of the organization. Amazon attributed the changes to efficiency and alignment with its product plans. This round is distinct from the earlier October reductions in the retail organization. No public restructuring charge or individual worksite count is established in the sources checked.
  • The reductions followed a series of hardware announcements. Amazon’s own Kindle launch page documents a redesigned Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft family, providing context for the division’s continuing product activity.
  • A separate engineering leadership memo discusses how software developers should use AI while being assessed on customer and business outcomes. It does not attribute this particular layoff round to AI, so no such causal claim or AI-layoff classification is assigned here.
  • The map uses Amazon’s Seattle headquarters campus as an estimated location anchor because the affected offices were not specified. The three Amazon gallery photos show the campus exterior, the Spheres at night and a decorative Amazon logo; they are archival context, not documentation of the notifications or affected workers.
